AppRef.description: The application this capability was recorded against.

vendor_product.description: Product identifier, e.g. acme-core-servicing or dolibarr.
vendor_product.title: Vendor Product

product_version.description: Product version observed at record time, if detectable.
product_version.title: Product Version

tenant_id.description: Tenant this capability is specialised for. None means it is the base.
tenant_id.title: Tenant Id

base_capability_id.description: For a tenant specialisation, the id of the base capability it derives from.
base_capability_id.title: Base Capability Id

AppRef.title: AppRef

CapabilityPolicy.description: Per-capability safety limits, layered on top of the global policy file.

allowed_hosts.description: Host patterns this capability may reach. Empty means inherit the global policy.
allowed_hosts.title: Allowed Hosts

allowed_routes.description: Route patterns this capability may reach. Empty means inherit the global policy.
allowed_routes.title: Allowed Routes

max_steps.description: Ceiling on steps executed during one replay.
max_steps.title: Max Steps

max_wall_clock_seconds.description: Ceiling on wall-clock time for one replay.
max_wall_clock_seconds.title: Max Wall Clock Seconds

CapabilityPolicy.title: CapabilityPolicy

Condition.description:
A testable claim about the current screen.

One type serves two jobs: as a step's checkpoint it asserts the step worked, and as an
outcome's detector it recognises a situation. They are the same question asked for
different reasons, so they are the same type.

kind.description: What is being checked: control_present, control_absent, text_present, url_matches, or value_equals.
kind.title: Kind

params.description: Arguments for the check. control_present/absent: role, name. text_present: text. url_matches: pattern. value_equals: role, name, value.
params.title: Params

negate.description: Whether to invert the result of the check.
negate.title: Negate

Condition.title: Condition

ControlDescriptor.description:
A control, described by what it is plus every way we know to find it.

The candidate list is the point. Recording one locator per control produces an artifact
that breaks on the first UI change; recording a ranked chain produces one that degrades.

role.description: Accessibility role of the control: button, textbox, link, cell, combobox.
role.title: Role

name.description: Accessible name of the control, if it has one. None where nothing is named.
name.title: Name

candidates.description: Ranked locator candidates, strongest first. The resolver walks them in order and records which one actually fired, so a non-primary candidate firing is a drift signal. Ordering is maintained by the model, not by the caller.
candidates.title: Candidates

ControlDescriptor.title: ControlDescriptor

EntryPoint.description: Where the flow starts, so replay can reach the same screen discovery began on.

url.description: Absolute url the flow starts from.
url.title: Url

requires_authenticated_session.description: Whether an authenticated session must already exist. Authentication is out of scope: replay attaches to a session that is already signed in.
requires_authenticated_session.title: Requires Authenticated Session

EntryPoint.title: EntryPoint

Locator.description:
One way to find a control, with an honest estimate of how well it will age.

A locator is a candidate, never the answer. `ControlDescriptor` holds several and the
resolver tries them in order, so a single brittle strategy failing is survivable.

strategy.description: How to find the control. role_name uses the accessibility role and name; anchor_relative locates it by its relationship to nearby text and is the primary strategy on legacy surfaces; region_ordinal falls back to position within a named region; text_content matches visible text and is brittle to localisation; dom_hint is a css or xpath selector and a terminal fallback.
strategy.title: Strategy

params.description: Strategy-specific arguments. role_name: role, name, match. anchor_relative: anchor_text, anchor_role, relation (same_row|following|within_region), target_role, index. region_ordinal: region, role, index. text_content: text, match. dom_hint: css or xpath.
params.title: Params

stability_score.description: Heuristic 0-1 estimate of how well this candidate survives UI change. Scored, not measured: named and anchor-based candidates score higher, index-dependent and generated-id-dependent ones lower, and surface-specific ones are capped.
stability_score.title: Stability Score

verified_unique_at_record.description: Whether this candidate was re-resolved against the live page at record time and matched exactly one node. A false here means the candidate was kept without proof and should not be trusted as a primary.
verified_unique_at_record.title: Verified Unique At Record

binds.description: Params whose value comes from a capability parameter at invocation, as {param_key: parameter_name}. A locator anchored on data that varies per call - 'the cell in the same row as the member id' - is structural, but only if the anchor is the caller's id rather than the one seen at record time. Without this the candidate silently works for exactly one input. The literal kept in `params` is what was seen when it was recorded, and is overwritten per call.
binds.title: Binds

surface_specific.description: Whether this candidate only works on the surface it was recorded against. True for dom_hint and nothing else. A non-web resolver skips these entirely, which is what keeps the artifact portable (C3).
surface_specific.title: Surface Specific

Locator.title: Locator

Outcome.description:
A situation the capability knows how to recognise, and what it means.

`kind` is the load-bearing type in this project. The brief names conflating a business
answer with a system failure as the most common design mistake, so the distinction lives
in the type system rather than in a convention:

- **business** - a legitimate answer the caller asked for. "No such member" is a result,
  not an exception. Returns status=business_outcome.
- **recoverable** - a condition replay handles and continues past: a known interstitial,
  one bounded retry on a transient load.
- **hard_failure** - stop, capture evidence, return something debuggable. Unknown page
  state, a checkpoint that failed with no matching detector, an exhausted locator chain.

name.description: Stable identifier for this outcome, e.g. member_not_found.
name.title: Name

kind.description: business: a legitimate answer for the caller, returned as a result rather than an error. recoverable: handled and continued past. hard_failure: stop and surface a debuggable error.
kind.title: Kind

detect.description: The condition that identifies this outcome on screen.

applies_to.description: Step ids this outcome can occur on, or 'any' when it can happen anywhere in the flow, as a session timeout can.
applies_to.title: Applies To

recovery.description: How to recover. Permitted only when kind is recoverable.

message_template.description: Human-readable explanation, returned to the caller with the result.
message_template.title: Message Template

partial_outputs.description: Names of declared outputs that are still valid when this outcome fires. A business outcome often carries real data even though the flow stopped early.
partial_outputs.title: Partial Outputs

Outcome.title: Outcome

OutputSpec.description: A value the capability promises to return, and where in the flow it comes from.

name.description: Output name, as it appears in the result's outputs map.
name.title: Name

type.description: Value type of the extracted output.
type.title: Type

source_step_id.description: Id of the step whose extraction produces this output.
source_step_id.title: Source Step Id

description.description: What this output means to the caller.
description.title: Description

sensitive.description: Whether the value is sensitive. Sensitive outputs are returned to the caller but never written to evidence or logs.
sensitive.title: Sensitive

OutputSpec.title: OutputSpec

ParamRef.description:
A step value that comes from a caller-supplied parameter rather than a constant.

Sensitive values reach a step only through one of these, which is what keeps them out
of the artifact: the artifact records the reference, never the value.

param.description: Name of the parameter whose value to use.
param.title: Param

ParamRef.title: ParamRef

Parameter.description:
An input the caller supplies when invoking the capability.

`sensitive` is a persistence control, not a display hint. A sensitive value is supplied
per invocation and must never reach an artifact, a log, an evidence file or a stability
record. The model enforces the part it can: a sensitive parameter cannot carry an example.

name.description: Parameter name, as used in step values via a ParamRef.
name.title: Name

type.description: Value type: string, integer, number, boolean or date (ISO 8601).
type.title: Type

required.description: Whether the caller must supply this parameter.
required.title: Required

sensitive.description: Whether the value is sensitive. A sensitive value is never persisted to the artifact, the run log, evidence or the stability record. It is supplied per invocation and dropped afterwards.
sensitive.title: Sensitive

description.description: What this parameter means, read by an agent deciding how to call this.
description.title: Description

example.description: A sample value, to show an agent the expected shape. Always null for a sensitive parameter: an example of a real account number is a real account number.
example.title: Example

Parameter.title: Parameter

Provenance.description:
Where this capability came from and whether a human has signed it off.

Unattended replay requires state='approved' and outcomes_reviewed=True. A model
proposes outcomes; it does not get to approve its own error taxonomy.

discovered_at.description: When the discovery run that produced this ran.
discovered_at.title: Discovered At

model.description: Model identifier that drove the discovery run.
model.title: Model

discovery_run_id.description: Id of the discovery run, linking this artifact to its evidence on disk.
discovery_run_id.title: Discovery Run Id

state.description: draft until a human reviews it; approved once signed off. Drift can demote an approved capability back to draft.
state.title: State

approved_by.description: Who approved it. Null while the state is draft.
approved_by.title: Approved By

outcomes_reviewed.description: Whether a human has reviewed the proposed outcomes. Required for unattended replay: the error taxonomy is the part a model is least trustworthy about.
outcomes_reviewed.title: Outcomes Reviewed

Provenance.title: Provenance

Recovery.description: What to do about a recoverable outcome, and how many times to try it.

action.description: The remedy: dismiss_dialog closes a known interstitial, retry_step repeats the step, wait_and_retry pauses first, reauthenticate re-establishes the session.
action.title: Action

max_attempts.description: How many times the remedy may be applied before this becomes a failure.
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

target.description: The control the remedy acts on, where it needs one (a dialog's close button).

Recovery.title: Recovery

StabilityRecord.description: Measured evidence that replay is deterministic, rather than a claim that it is.

runs.description: How many replays this record summarises.
runs.title: Runs

passes.description: How many of those replays succeeded.
passes.title: Passes

locator_usage.description: Per control, how often each locator strategy actually fired. A non-primary strategy appearing here is the earliest visible sign of UI drift.
locator_usage.title: Locator Usage

recoveries.description: Per step, how many runs needed a recovery. This is the baseline that makes 'a recoverable outcome that never fired before' answerable rather than guessed.
recoveries.title: Recoveries

drift_signals.description: Observations suggesting the surface has moved: a fallback candidate firing, or a recoverable outcome triggering on a step that never needed it before.
drift_signals.title: Drift Signals

StabilityRecord.title: StabilityRecord

Step.description: One action in the recorded flow, with the check that proves it worked.

id.description: Stable identifier for this step, referenced by outcomes.
id.title: Id

intent.description: What this step is for, in human terms: 'search for the member'.
intent.title: Intent

action.description: The action to perform: navigate, click, type, select, press_key, wait_for, extract or assert.
action.title: Action

target.description: The control acted on. None for actions that need no control, like navigate.

value.description: The value for the action: a literal string, or a ParamRef naming a parameter supplied at invocation. Sensitive values are always references, never literals.
value.title: Value

checkpoint.description: Condition asserted after the action. A checkpoint that fails with no matching outcome detector is a hard failure.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for this step before giving up.
timeout_ms.title: Timeout Ms

risk_class.description: Risk of this step, gated by the policy engine. safe: reads and navigation. risky: submits, saves, creates. irreversible: deletes, transfers, disbursements - always blocked and escalated to a human, never model-approved.
risk_class.title: Risk Class

Step.title: Step

description:
A reusable, typed, versioned recording of how to accomplish one goal in a UI.

This is what the whole system exists to produce. Discovery writes one; replay executes
it with no model in the decision loop; the catalog exposes it to an agent as a callable
tool. Its JSON Schema, exported by `export.py`, is the agent-facing contract.

schema_version.description: Version of this artifact format, for forward compatibility.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

description.description: What this capability does, written for an agent deciding whether to call it. This is the text a model reads when choosing between capabilities.
description.title: Description

version.description: Semantic version, bumped whenever the steps change.
version.title: Version

app.description: The application and tenant this was recorded against.

surface_kind.description: Kind of surface this capability drives.
surface_kind.title: Surface Kind

parameters.description: Inputs the caller supplies at invocation.
parameters.title: Parameters

outputs.description: Values the capability returns on success.
outputs.title: Outputs

outcomes.description: Situations this capability recognises, and what each one means.
outcomes.title: Outcomes

stability.description: Measured replay stability, once it has been measured.

title: Capability
